body.p: lets you organize DITA resources into projects, just as you do with other files. Projects help you manage and organize files, perform batch operations (such as validations and transformations) on multiple files, and use Main Files support to rename or move DITA resources while updating their references. You can also share your project settings and transformation/validation scenarios with other users.
To learn how to create a new project from a template, add resources, and manage the project, see .

Several DITA project templates are available to help you become familiar with working with DITA projects. Access them using the New Project action (available, for example, from the Project menu). They are located in the Framework templates DITA folder of the wizard. A description is displayed when you select a template.

section.title: DITA Project Templates
section.p: The following templates provide starting points for your documentation. They include a minimal or placeholder structure that you replace with your own content:

row.entry: The smallest DITA project, with one map and a single topic, ready to publish to WebHelp and PDF. Use it to build your own structure.
A placeholder user guide for a software product (installation, configuration, common tasks, troubleshooting, and FAQs). Set your product name once, then publish to WebHelp and PDF.

A user guide written in Markdown, with Markdown topics that contain YAML metadata, organized in a DITA map and published to WebHelp and PDF. It starts with a complete sample guide for a cloud CRM, including procedures, a reference, release notes, key references, and reused notes. Set your product name once, then replace the sample topics with your own.

A blog written in DITA, with one topic per post, categories defined in the map, and the author and date stored in the topic prolog. It publishes to a WebHelp website with a home page that lists the latest posts, category filters, and an RSS feed.

AI skills written in Markdown and organized as a Claude Code plugin marketplace. Each skill is a SKILL.md file, grouped into plugins by area, and users can install the plugins directly from the repository without a build step. A DITA map lists the skills so that you can edit and publish them as a catalog. It starts with sample skills for release notes, terminology, and support replies.

AI skills written in DITA and published to Markdown as a Claude Code plugin marketplace. Each skill becomes a SKILL.md file, grouped into plugins by area. Because the skills are written in DITA, they can reuse content. Product names come from keys, and instructions shared by several skills are written only once. It starts with sample skills for release notes, terminology, and support replies.

A writing style guide for your documentation team, covering voice and tone, formatting, code, and terminology rules. Each rule includes the reason behind it, along with examples to avoid and examples to follow. It publishes to WebHelp and PDF, for writers to consult.
The Software Guide template in English, German, and French, organized for translation, with one folder per language, a combined multilingual map, and outputs for each language.

A DITA project that applies a custom set of options (for example, spell-check settings and custom dictionaries), a custom DITA framework extension (for example, custom new-file templates, custom actions, custom Schematron validation rules, and custom CSS for visual editing), terminology checking rules, publishing settings, and a folder structure that follows DITA project best practices. Once created, the project contains a README.md file that explains the customizations and their benefits. If you plan to create a DITA project that uses a version control system (such as Git), you can use this template to customize various aspects of DITA editing and share them with your team.

section.p: The following templates create complete sample projects that demonstrate various DITA features and can provide inspiration:

row.entry: A complete manual for a fictional chat application, published as separate User and Admin guides (WebHelp and PDF) through audience filtering. It demonstrates content reuse through content references, keys, and a relationship table.
A developer guide for a sample weather REST API, with getting started, authentication, rate limits, webhooks, and release notes topics. The API reference is generated from an OpenAPI 3.0 file.
A user guide for two smartphone models, written once and filtered per model and audience, plus a combined catalog of both models. It demonstrates keys, key scopes, and variant publishing.

A small gardening guide about flowers organized by season, with care tasks and a glossary, published to WebHelp with a custom look. It demonstrates faceted search, built from a subject scheme map and a classification map, as well as search labels that identify each plant as perennial or annual.

A service and parts manual for an industrial hydraulic pump in English, German, and French, with a clickable exploded view, specifications, maintenance procedures, safety warnings, and a PDF output for each language.

section.p: The sample projects, along with the Markdown User Guide, are also available in the dita subfolder of the samples project (samples/sample.xpr) in the installation directory, ready to be opened.

In addition, the Policies & Procedures - Governance project template, located in the Framework templates Governance folder, enables you to define policies and SOPs for your company. It includes preconfigured publishing scenarios and AI Skills that help you create content more easily while following the file template structure.

section.title: Resources
section.p: For more information about working with DITA projects, see our webinar: Working with DITA in Oxygen - Quick Start with the DITA Startup Project.
